# std::linalg::spectral

<!-- Generated by scripts/check_spec.py from docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml. Edit that file and run `python3 scripts/check_spec.py --write`. -->

The properties of the exact spectral profile of polynomial matrix fields, from ADR 0001 §12. Let A be the ring of the polynomials with exact rational coefficients in the coordinates of a smooth affine object X. A free module V on X is Aⁿ with a named basis, with n at most 4, and an endomorphism field H of V is an n × n matrix over A. The spectral pair of H has the characteristic polynomial χ = det(tI − H) in A[t], with a named fiber coordinate t, and the module V on which t acts as H. A branch is a finite chart D(g) of the spectrum, certified by a witness W with W·χ′ ≡ gᵉ modulo χ, on which every eigenvalue is simple. The module declares the families `FreeModule<X>`, `Endomorphism<X>`, `Spectrum<X>` and `Branch<X>`. The application declares each module, field, spectrum and branch, the invariants `trace_power` and `char_coefficient`, and the observations `annihilates`, `action_entry`, `on_branch`, `branch_differential` and `branch_projector`. The failure value ⊥ lies over no point.

[Specifications](../specifications.md) defines the [claim statuses](../specifications.md#claim-statuses) and the checks. This chapter is generated from [`docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/docs/spec/std-linalg-spectral.toml).

<a id="spectral.static-identity"></a>

## Objects and spectra are static

- Property: `spectral.static-identity`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

A field acts on a free module of its own object, a spectrum is the spectrum of a field of its own object, and a branch is a chart of a spectrum of its own object; any other declaration is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`). An observation names its spectrum or its branch in its binding. It accepts a point only of the object of that spectrum or branch, and a branch observation accepts an eigenvalue only on its declared line. Any other operand is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`).

- Example: On the plane, let H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)) act on V = basis(e1, e2). A field `rows((u, v), (v, −u))` of V on a second plane with the coordinates u and v is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`), although both planes have the dimension 2. An observation of the spectrum of the field 2I on the point, applied to a point of the plane, is an error (`E_ENDPOINT`).
- Run by: `spectral_mismatches_are_rejected_statically` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.pair"></a>

## The spectral pair is computed and checked

- Property: `spectral.pair`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

For a spectrum `eigen(H, t)` the kernel computes χ = det(tI − H) and adj(tI − H), and accepts the declaration only when χ equals the cofactor determinant of tI − H, (tI − H)·adj = adj·(tI − H) = χ·I, the trace of the adjugate is χ′, χ(H) = 0, adj² − χ′·adj is a multiple of χ, and Jacobi's formula ∂ᵢχ + tr(adj·∂ᵢH) = 0 holds for each coordinate. Every identity modulo χ is checked against a quotient that the kernel computes. No characteristic polynomial, adjugate or quotient comes from the source or the wire.

- Example: For H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)) the kernel computes χ = t² − x² − y² and adj(tI − H) = tI + H. A spectrum record with a field `characteristic`, `adjugate` or `quotient` is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).
- Run by: `raw_wire_rejects_spectral_certificates_and_forged_maps` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.module-action"></a>

## The module action tells fields apart

- Property: `spectral.module-action`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Spectrum`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

`annihilates(…, spectrum = S, element = f)` at a point p is true exactly when f(H(p)) = 0, and `action_entry(…, spectrum = S, element = f, eᵢ, eⱼ)` is the entry (eᵢ, eⱼ) of f(H(p)), for f in A[t]. The spectrum is the characteristic scheme of H, never its reduced spectrum or the locus of an annihilator: two fields with the same χ, the same trace powers and the same coefficients can differ in their module action.

- Example: On the point, 2I and J = [[2, 1], [0, 2]] both have χ = (t − 2)², the trace powers 4 and 8 and the same coefficients. t − 2 annihilates 2I and not J, and the entry (f1, f2) of J − 2I is 1, that of 2I − 2I is 0. (t − 2)² annihilates both (Cayley–Hamilton). The fields 0 and N = [[0, 1], [0, 0]] differ in the same way.
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_shows_no_failures_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

<a id="spectral.invariants"></a>

## Invariants are smooth maps

- Property: `spectral.invariants`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Endomorphism`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

`trace_power(H, k)`, for 1 ≤ k ≤ 8, is the smooth map tr(Hᵏ) from the object of H to a line, and `char_coefficient(S, i)` is the coefficient of tⁱ in χ. Each is an ordinary smooth map: its differential, its gradient under a metric and its compiled reverse pass are those of `std::differential`, and it has no reverse rule of its own. The kernel computes the map from the declaration; a map on the wire is an error (`E_PROTOCOL`).

- Example: For H = rows((x, y), (y, −x)), `trace_power(H, 2)` is the map 2x² + 2y², equal to the map `pullback(t -> 2*x^2 + 2*y^2)`. Its gradient on the dimensionless Euclidean chart is (4x, 4y): (4, 8) at (1, 2) and (0, 0) at the origin. tr(H) is 0, whose differential is the zero covector over the point and not ⊥, and the coefficient of t⁰ is −x² − y², whose gradient is −1/2 that of tr(H²).
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_shows_no_failures_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

  - Assumes: [mathlib](assumptions.md#assumption.mathlib), [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: `toMv_tracePower` states that an accepted trace power is the trace of the k-th power of the field over `MvPolynomial (Fin m) ℚ`, and `realProgram_tracePower` that its real map is y ↦ tr(H(y)ᵏ). For a symmetric field `tracePower_fderiv_dk` states that its derivative read with the covector 1 is the Daleckii–Krein cotangent `dkCotangent (· ^ k) (hermAt M hM y) (trPairing 1)` composed with `hermDeriv M hM y`. `checked_trace_power_dk` states that an accepted `differential` node of the invariant computes that covector, and `compiled_trace_power_dk`, `public_resource_entries_trace_power_dk` and `public_pure_entry_trace_power_dk` that every compiled reverse site of one declared step along it, in every compiled module and on the public paths of protocols 8 and 9, computes the seed's component times it. `stage5_dk_gradient` states that for the field of the example, as a Mathlib matrix, the cotangent is (4y₀, 4y₁) at every real point; no theorem composes it with `checked_trace_power_dk` (#813). `lean-bridge/Audit.lean` checks that the theorems about accepted Core reach no chain-rule theorem.

<a id="spectral.branch-chart"></a>

## A branch is a certified finite chart

- Property: `spectral.branch-chart`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Branch`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Negative tests](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#negative-tests-2)

`simple(S, localize = g, witness = W, exponent = e)` is accepted only when g is a nonzero polynomial in the coordinates of the object, without the fiber coordinate, W has degree below n in t, e ≤ 8, and W·χ′ − gᵉ is a multiple of χ, which the kernel checks against a quotient that it computes. Any other chart is an error (`E_SPECTRAL`). On D(g), in every commutative ring that receives the rationals, χ′ is a unit wherever χ vanishes, so every eigenvalue of H(p) is simple.

- Example: For χ = t² − x² − y², the witness t/2 certifies D(x² + y²): (t/2)·2t = t² is x² + y² modulo χ. The same witness with g = 1 is an error, because the eigenvalues meet at the origin, and so is the witness (1/2 + 10⁻²⁰)t. The Jordan block [[2, 1], [0, 2]] has no chart, because χ′ = 2(t − 2) is nilpotent modulo χ = (t − 2)².
- Run by: `rejected_stage5_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `rejected_stage5_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)
    - `tampered_spectral_declarations_are_rejected_by_the_kernel` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)
    - `powers_and_exponents_are_bounded` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - [`VastitasKernel.SpectralDeclarationRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/SpectralDeclarationRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
  - Note: The rejected packages `spectral-gap-at-origin`, `spectral-jordan-branch` and `spectral-wrong-witness` print their diagnostics. The tampered wire gives the branch of the example the localization 1, 0 and t, a perturbed witness and an unreduced one.
- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralDeclarations.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.checkWitness_sound`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.WitnessValid.gap_at`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.SpectralValid.unit_at`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.SpectralValid.derivative_ne_zero`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.branch_sound`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.Examples.origin_off_chart`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.Examples.unit_gap_no_witness`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance.c8_gap_certificate`
  - Premises:
    - for `SpectralValid.unit_at` and `SpectralValid.derivative_ne_zero`: the certificate and the gap witness are valid, which `branch_sound` proves for every branch of a valid environment, and χ vanishes at the point, where g has an inverse, or is not zero for the rational form
    - for `WitnessValid.gap_at`: χ has the arity of the object and the fiber coordinate
    - for `branch_sound` and `c8_gap_certificate`: the declaration environment is valid
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: `checkWitness_sound` states that an accepted chart has a nonzero localization without the fiber coordinate, a reduced witness, an exponent of at most 8 and W·χ′ − gᵉ = Q·χ, and `gap_at` that the identity holds at every point of every ring. `unit_at` states that where χ vanishes and g has an inverse u, χ′ has the inverse W·uᵉ, so over ℚ χ′ ≠ 0 at a branch point; no theorem instantiates `unit_at` at the complex eigenvalues of a real point (#813). `unit_gap_no_witness` states that the localization 1 has no witness, exponent and quotient at all for the field of the example: at (0, 0, ε) in the dual numbers χ = ε² = 0 and g = 1, so χ′ = 2ε would be a unit. `origin_off_chart` states that every localization that the gap check accepts for that χ vanishes at the origin. The rejections of the Jordan block and of the perturbed witness are decided for those inputs in `c8_gap_certificate`. These statements are about the literal χ and g of the example, not about a declared branch (#813).

<a id="spectral.branch-observations"></a>

## Branch points, differentials and eigenprojectors

- Property: `spectral.branch-observations`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::Branch`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Laws](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#laws-2)

Let p be a point and t a rational on the line. `on_branch` is true exactly when g(p) ≠ 0 and χ(p, t) = 0. At such a branch point, `branch_differential` is the covector −Σᵢ (∂ᵢχ / χ′)(p, t) dxᵢ, and `branch_projector` with eᵢ and eⱼ is the entry (eᵢ, eⱼ) of adj(tI − H(p)) / χ′(p, t). Off the chart the differential is ⊥ and an entry reads (0, 0). No observation computes, orders or chooses an eigenvalue.

- Example: At p = (3, 4) the eigenvalues 5 and −5 are on the branch of D(x² + y²), and 4 is not; the origin is off the chart, although χ(0, 0) = 0 at t = 0. The differentials are (3/5, 4/5) and (−3/5, −4/5), unit covectors under the Euclidean metric, and the eigenprojectors are (1/5)[[4, 2], [2, 1]] and (1/5)[[1, −2], [−2, 4]].
- Run by: `the_example_checks_builds_and_shows_no_failures_in_place` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)

Claims:

- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:

    - `mutated_observations_change_the_native_result` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)
    - `spectral_families_from_the_library_check_build_and_run_from_a_path_package` in [`tests/stdlib_spectral.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/stdlib_spectral.rs)

On the branch P·P = P, tr P = 1 and H(p)·P = P·H(p) = t·P, which `c11_eigenprojector` states for an accepted call, a column with Pⱼⱼ ≠ 0 is an eigenvector of H(p) for t, the components of the differential satisfy cᵢ·χ′(p, t) = −∂ᵢχ(p, t), and cᵢ = tr(P·∂ᵢH(p)). The components are built from the evaluated partial derivatives of χ, never from a reverse pass. `c9_branch_points` decides the branch points of the example. That P is symmetric for a symmetric field is tested, not stated: it would follow from identifying the certificate's adjugate with `Matrix.adjugate`. That such a λ exists, by the implicit function theorem, is not claimed. `branch_mem_spectrum` states that a real zero of χ is an eigenvalue of H(x), and `unit_witness_localization` that ∂ₜχ is a unit in the localization away from g of ℚ[x, t]/(χ).

<a id="spectral.limits"></a>

## The finite profile

- Property: `spectral.limits`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral::FreeModule`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Execution and evidence profile](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#execution-and-evidence-profile-2)

A free module has at most 4 basis vectors (`spectralRank`), and a trace power and the exponent of a branch are at most 8 (`spectralPower`). Every polynomial that the kernel reads or computes for a field, a spectral pair, a trace power or a witness check is within the term limit, and its computation within the work budget, of the exact algebra. Beyond a limit the declaration is an error (`E_LIMIT`), reported before any identity is compared.

- Example: A free module with the basis e1, …, e5 is an error (`E_LIMIT`), and so is `trace_power(H, 9)`. A symmetric 4 × 4 field whose entries are the 455-term polynomial (1 + x0 + … + x11)³ stops on the work budget while its spectral pair is computed.
- Run by: `the_rank_is_bounded_at_the_free_module` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance.c1_fields_and_modules`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance.c12_degenerate`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralDeclarations.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.checkModule_sound`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.invariant_sound`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralDeclarations.checkWitness_sound`
  - Premises:
    - for `c1_fields_and_modules`: the declaration environment is valid
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: The theorems state the soundness half of the profile: an accepted free module has 1 to 4 distinct basis names, an accepted field has a rank of at most 4, an accepted trace power and an accepted exponent are at most 8, and `c12_degenerate` decides that a field of rank 4 is accepted and one of rank 5 is not. That a declaration beyond a limit is rejected with `E_LIMIT` before any identity is compared, and within seconds, is tested. The budgets hold for each declaration, and no budget bounds a whole program (#769). The polynomial of a trace-power invariant is computed once in each pass over the program, not at each call of it (#812).
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - `the_rank_is_bounded_at_the_free_module` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - `powers_and_exponents_are_bounded` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - `terms_are_bounded_before_any_comparison` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - `the_spectral_pair_is_bounded_by_the_work_budget` in [`tests/spectral_limits.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_limits.rs)
    - `rejected_stage5_packages_print_their_diagnostics` in [`tests/spectral_observations.rs`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/tests/spectral_observations.rs)
  - Note: Each check of `tests/spectral_limits.rs` ends within 30 seconds, and each rejected one reports its `E_LIMIT` instead of the error of the comparison that the limit guards.

<a id="spectral.weakening"></a>

## Spectral declarations change nothing else

- Property: `spectral.weakening`
- Subject: `std::linalg::spectral`
- Rule: [ADR 0001 §12, Contract and jurisdiction](../adr/0001-mathematics-first-stdlib.md#contract-and-jurisdiction-2)

A free module, a field, a spectrum or a branch changes neither the validity of a declaration of another kind nor the validity or the value of a primitive that names none of these declarations, the primitives of smooth geometry, metrics and frames included. No spectral primitive reads a metric, a frame or a physical dimension, and each evaluates the same in every environment.

- Example: The metric `Euclid`, its evidence and `sharp` of the acceptance program have the same validity and values with and without the free modules, fields, spectra and branches of the program, and a program without observations or invariants is accepted on its own.
- Run by: [`VastitasKernel.SpectralRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/SpectralRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)

Claims:

- `oracle`: [Proved (oracle)](../specifications.md#proved-oracle)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralWeakening.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.spectral_weakening_binding`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.spectral_weakening_entry`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.stage4_bindings_spectral_free`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.spectral_bindings_metric_free`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.spectral_bindings_frame_free`, `VastitasOracle.SpectralWeakening.spectral_bindings_nature_free`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralCore`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralCore.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralCore.spectral_bindings_environment_free`
    - [`VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean/VastitasOracle/SpectralAcceptance.lean): `VastitasOracle.SpectralAcceptance.c13_weakening`
  - Premises:
    - the environment with the added declarations has unique ids
    - for `spectral_weakening_binding`: the binding names none of the added declarations
    - for `spectral_bindings_frame_free`: the binding names no frame
  - Assumes: [Rust frontend parsing](assumptions.md#assumption.rust-frontend)
  - Note: The declaration statements hold for every table of class ranks. That the kernel computes the same table of class ranks with and without the added declarations is not proved, so the statements are not stated for the validity of a whole program. The four families of the module are not among the added declarations (#813).
- `test`: [Tested](../specifications.md#tested)
  - Evidence:
    - [`VastitasKernel.SpectralRegression`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/lean-kernel/VastitasKernel/SpectralRegression.lean), built by [`scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh`](https://github.com/MGYamada/Vastitas/blob/main/scripts/check_kernel_regressions.sh)
